chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad said: Ubaydullah ibn Musa al-Alawi narrated to us from Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abut-Tufayl, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him): That
Ibn Abbas sent someone to ask him about this verse: "O you who believe! Be patient and excel in patience and remain steadfast and fear Allah, that you may succeed."

Ali ibn al-Husayn became angry and said to the messenger: "I wish that he who sent you with this had faced me with it himself." Then he said: "This verse was revealed about my father and us. The steadfastness (rabt) that we have been ordered to perform has not yet occurred; it will be for some of our descendants who remain steadfast." Then he said: "Indeed, in his loins (meaning Ibn Abbas) is a progeny created for the Fire of Hell. They will send forth great masses of people deviating from the religion of Allah. The earth will be dyed with the blood of the young ones from the young ones of the Family of Muhammad. Those young ones will rise in an unsuitable time and seek what is unattainable. The believers will remain steadfast and persevere until Allah judges, and He is the best of judges."

key_terms.رَبَاطٌ: Steadfastness or remaining stationed/guarding, often in a military or spiritual context
key_terms.صَابِرُوا: Excelling in patience or urging others to patience
key_terms.فَرَخٌ: Young one or offspring, used here for the descendants of the Prophet's family

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the command to 'remain steadfast' (rabt) in Surah Al-Imran verse 200 according to Imam Sajjad?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (as) clarifies that while the command for 'Sabr' (patience) and 'Rabat' (steadfastness/guarding) in Surah Al-Imran was revealed regarding him and his father, the specific military or guarding aspect ('Rabat') is a future duty of their descendants, particularly the Mahdi. This narration highlights the Shia eschatological view of active vigilance rather than passive waiting, linking the verse to the eventual rise of the Ahl al-Bayt against deviant factions emerging from the progeny of Ibn Abbas.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (12) Ali bin Ahmad narrated from Obaydillah bin Musa al-Alawi from Ali bin Ibraheem bin Hashim from Ali bin Issma’eel from Hammad bin Eessa from Ibraheem bin Umar al-Yamani from Abut-Tufayl that Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ali al-Baqir (as) had said:
Once ibn Abbas sent a messenger to Ali bin al-Husayn as-Sajjad (as) asking him about this Qur’anic verse, “O you who believe! Be patient and excel in patience and remain steadfast.”

Ali bin al-Husayn (as) became angry and said to the messenger: “I wish that he, who has sent you with this, faced me with it.” Then he said: “This verse has been revealed about my father and us. Perseverance that we have been ordered of has not occurred yet. It will be for some of our descendants.” Then he added: “From his (ibn Abbas’s) progeny there are some descendants created to be in Hell. They will deviate great masses of people from the religion of Allah. The earth will be dyed with the blood of the descendants of Muhammad’s progeny. Those descendants will rise in unsuitable times and ask for unattainable things. The believers will remain steadfast and persevere until Allah determines and He is the best of judges.”
